title: Secure SDK auth primitives: API key lifecycle, SSO token refresh, and secret-handling guidance
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Implement a cross-language (Python/TypeScript/Go) set of SDK primitives and best-practice guidance for authentication and secret handling. Work covers: 1) API key usage patterns and safe defaults (env-only loading, in-memory rotation hooks, scoped keys), 2) key rotation flows with zero-downtime refresh for long-lived processes, 3) SSO token acquisition/refresh for enterprise customers (OIDC/SAML exchange examples), 4) secret handling guidance for deployments (local dev, CI/CD, Dedicated, Private), and 5) small ergonomic helpers for streaming auth headers and retry-safe credential refresh during streaming. Deliver docs, examples, integration tests, and a security review checklist.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (py/ts/go) expose a single secure credential loader that supports API_KEY, file-based service credentials, and short-lived SSO tokens
Rotation helper that can be registered with long-running processes to swap credentials without dropping in-flight requests
Enterprise guide with concrete OIDC/SAML token exchange examples and a sample implementation for automatic refresh in SDKs
Docs and code examples for secure local development, CI secrets, and Dedicated/Private deployment patterns
End-to-end tests demonstrating token refresh under streaming (server and client), with no auth leakage in logs
Security review completed and any findings addressed before merge

notes: Trade-offs: We could rely solely on cloud KMS/secret manager SDKs, but this ticket aims to provide consistent cross-cloud patterns and an opinionated loader for customers who run in Private/Dedicated environments.

Streaming ergonomics: For JS SDK, prefer a middleware approach where a header-resolver async function is called per-stream-chunk boundary; for Python and Go, prefer context-bound token provider with atomic swap to avoid locking on hot paths.

Open questions: Revocation flow for active tokens — should server send an explicit 401 that triggers rotation, or should SDK proactively poll token metadata? Decided to support both, prefer reactive 401-driven refresh with backoff as default.
Rollback plan: Feature behind 'auth-v2' flag. If token refresh causes instability we will revert flag and ship minimal docs updates only.
